implementation_notes: Do not hand-roll this in C#. The BCL provides ConcurrentQueue, ConcurrentDictionary, ConcurrentBag and a lock-free stack - ConcurrentQueue and ConcurrentDictionary are documented as lock-free - all audited over years of production use. Interlocked gives the primitive if you need it. A general progress argument is nearly never justified on .NET: the GC's own pauses mean the worst-case latency is already bounded by something an order of magnitude larger than any lock-free algorithm's tail, so chasing lock-freedom does not improve the tail that users actually observe. Use System.Collections.Concurrent and spend the effort elsewhere.
pitfalls: ConcurrentQueue is lock-free but is not lock-free with respect to memory allocation - each enqueue allocates a segment, so GC pressure remains.
Interlocked on a single contended cache line is slower than a lock with batching; shard the counter before reaching for the primitive.
The lock-free collection does not make the surrounding code thread-safe: shared mutable state outside the collection is still your problem.
A thread abort or a ThreadAbortException mid-operation can leave a structure in a state the algorithm assumed a thread would complete - helping protocols help with stalls, not with aborts.
alternative: System.Collections.Concurrent collections and SemaphoreSlim/ReaderWriterLockSlim for blocking coordination; Channels<T> for producer-consumer hand-off
